mystery_dynamics.research.test.text:
In an age where technology reigns, we ought to move with the times.

But honestly, my colleagues' hidebound ways are unbearable. When running generators and other equipment, they only ever order golems to turn the crank, and would not even bother inventing dedicated devices for it. It is utterly pointless—hiring a few villagers would be more practical.

Fortunately, I have had quite a few ideas lately. Perhaps some of them can be put into practice, replacing these cumbersome devices with simpler, faster sources of power.
mystery_dynamics.research.straw_golem_po:
After some simple tinkering, you stripped the straw golem of its spare limbs, made a few improvements, and mounted it on a purpose-built base.

It can now output stress directly. Due to the material, however, this contraption currently provides only 128 SU of stress—but since the material is light enough, its speed reaches 160 RPM.
tc.research_text.CLAY_GOLEM_POWER: Is this really red brick and not blue brick?
tc.research_text.IRON_GOLEM_POWER: I think I need a wheelbarrow...
mystery_dynamics.research.wood_golem_pow:
Having practiced on the straw golem, you set about modifying the wooden one.

Happily, its material is sturdier and can withstand greater force, bringing the stress output to 256 SU.

For the same material reasons, though, it is bulkier than the straw version, so its speed is only 128 RPM.
mystery_dynamics.research.clay_golem_pow:
Likewise, you modified the clay golem. Hmm, a little brittle, but you managed it.

Compared with wood, the strength is raised again, and the stress output reaches 512 SU.

And thanks to the relatively light material, the speed stays at 128 RPM.
mystery_dynamics.research.stone_golem_po:
Would anyone actually make this thing? Still, since it is cheap enough, you built one for research.

Because of the material and its considerable weight, the stress output reaches a decent 1024 SU, but the speed drops to 64 RPM.
mystery_dynamics.research.iron_golem_pow:
This thing is much heavier than the stone one. In return, its output is twice that of stone, soaring straight to 2048 SU.

It really is heavy, though, so its speed is only 32 RPM.
mystery_dynamics.research.mystery_golem_:
Honestly, thaumium is as durable as they say. After a round of tinkering, you managed to build it right at the limit of its performance.

Pushing the material's performance threshold and using a large number of Air Shards, this machine's output reaches an astonishing 4096 SU.

Compared with iron, its speed is raised to 128 RPM.
tc.research_text.TALLOW_GOLEM_POWER: At least the fan needs no extra power
mystery_dynamics.research.flesh_golem_po:
After leafing through some books on living things, you decided to modify the flesh golem.

Creepy as it is, its low cost and decent performance are enough to cover up its other problems.

After fitting the golem with extra bones to serve as a transmission, its efficiency turns out to be quite good, with a stress output of 384 SU.

And thanks to the simple adjustments to its muscle structure, its speed reaches a rather good 160 RPM.
mystery_dynamics.research.tallow_golem_p:
Good news: this thing is slippery enough that its speed easily reaches 256 RPM.

Bad news: no matter how you tried, you could not improve its strength much, so you can only stick a wooden rod in as a transmission—hence only 128 SU.
mystery_dynamics.research.essentia_disti: Placeholder text: essentia distillation reference node.
mystery_dynamics.research.redstone_engin:
According to a paper someone shared, Redstone Flux can drive high-power engines to generate kinetic power without needing boilers or fuel—that sounds pretty good.

I thought I would try designing one myself, and this is the result. Just feed it Redstone Flux and adjust the signal to demand; it can output up to 8192 SU of stress and 256 RPM.

When I showed the design to others, their expressions were rather strange. I suppose there must be something unusual about my design.
mystery_dynamics.research.infernal_boile:
After deploying more machines, you find that the power at home is no longer enough.

So you turn your eyes to the Infernal Furnace that never stops working.

Using the Infernal Furnace's fuel-free principle as a foundation, you design this boiler. It provides three heat levels by default, needs no fuel at all, and can be heated further with vis and bellows just like the Infernal Furnace.

Notably, feeding it Fire essentia sends it into an overclocked state like a combustion chamber, doubling its output.

tc.research_text.LARGE_CENTRIFUGE: I said, are you deaf to balancing?!
mystery_dynamics.research.large_centrifu:
Those centrifuges are decent, but far too slow, and you have a batch of goods that needs to be finished urgently.

So you built a large version of the centrifuge. It can process a large amount of essentia at once, but due to some as-yet-unexplained issue, one batch can only produce a single type of essentia.

Fortunately, it can accept a much higher rotation speed to run faster. The price is a few small safety hazards.

And it seems quite a few people are interested in purchasing one, so you had better pry those golems out of the wall before they visit.
tc.research_text.NERIIDS_PROTECTION: The fifteenth day of the first lunar month is the Lantern Festival, the hour when the Heavenly Official of the Upper Prime bestows blessings.
mystery_dynamics.research.neriids_protec:
Deep-sea work is highly profitable, but the underwater part is always limited by breathing.

Bulky diving suits are too slow, while water breathing potions are too expensive as a long-term consumable. There was no relatively cheap alternative between the two, which made for a huge opportunity, so you designed this equipment to supply oxygen underwater.

You originally intended to call it the 'Integrated Underwater Oxygen Supply System', but market considerations led you to give it this name instead.
item.mystery_dynamics.high_pressure_laun: Launches any valid ammo from your inventory
Uses compressed air to negate durability loss
mystery_dynamics.research.high_pressure_:
Issuing firearms en masse to factory security and field survey teams is practically an invitation to rebellion. Fortunately, non-powder weapons face far looser regulation and licensing—an excellent opening.

You heavily modified the potato cannon, greatly improving air compression and instantaneous release, causing its power to surge. At the same time, you specially treated the barrel and chamber so that it is no longer limited to potatoes and carrots, allowing far more items to be used as ammunition.

Even before the strictest magistrate it is merely a high-pressure injector; but when loaded with metal or Alumentum, it is enough to remind anyone facing it what the law means.

The following additional ammunition is currently available:
Iron Nugget / Thaumium Nugget / Void Metal Nugget / Gold Nugget / Copper Nugget / Quicksilver Drop / Nitor / Alumentum / Chicken Nugget / Beef Nugget / Pork Nugget / Fish Nugget / Triple Meat Treat / Lightning Rod / Gold Coin / Void Seed / Tainted Goo

Ammunition with special effects:

Quicksilver Drop: Poison III for 10 seconds
Nitor: sets the target on fire for 10 seconds and grants Glowing for 15 seconds; places Nitor at the block impact point
Alumentum: explodes on impact
Triple Meat Treat: grants Regeneration on hit
Lightning Rod: strikes the target with lightning when conditions allow
Gold Coin: makes nearby piglins unusually hostile toward the struck creature
Tainted Goo: inflicts Flux Taint on the struck creature
Void Metal Nugget: inflicts Weakness
Void Seed: inflicts Wither

tc.research_text.ARCANE_TURBINE: Sorry, steam engine, we're not close
mystery_dynamics.research.arcane_turbine:
Honestly, the roar of a traditional steam engine is a disaster, and its efficiency is appalling.

To save your ears and your precious floor space, you borrowed a few principles from fluid dynamics and redesigned the whole apparatus so it wrings every last bit of energy out of high-pressure steam.

Now a mere handful of these turbines can steadily deliver the full stress output of an entire large boiler.

Best of all, it's quiet.
tc.research_text.MONEY_AND_POWER: They clearly have no idea how much wealth they produce
mystery_dynamics.research.money_and_powe:
The traditional workshop has always had an inherent flaw, at least as far as your ever-growing order book is concerned.

To meet a delivery deadline, you hired a few villagers for the basic work, more or less as an experiment. To your delight, the big-nosed fellows turned out to be remarkably handy. Production moved well ahead of schedule, and with only a modest cut of the profit they learned fast and soon took over part of the process.

Compared with your colleagues and their outrageous prices, these hmm-ing and haw-ing folk are clearly a bargain of a workforce, and they don't ask for much in return.

Time to say goodbye to those freeloaders for good.
mystery_dynamics.research.outsourcing_en:
Hiring villagers solved your labour shortage, but fixed wages alone will only push their productivity so far.

To really get them motivated, you changed the arrangement: instead of supervising production yourself, you hand them simplified equipment and basic materials and sign a legally binding outsourcing contract. You issue orders and supply materials; they deliver acceptable goods on time.

As for payment, forget those gold coins nobody accepts anyway. Settle up in the emeralds the big-noses love.
mystery_dynamics.research.thaumaturge_wo:
Many basic materials don't call for any deep arcane skill, just a lot of repetitive labour. So you picked out a batch of low-skill but exhausting tasks and licensed them to the big-noses.

Surprisingly, as long as they are paid on time, these villagers will happily toil away at the workstation all day long and turn out materials with remarkable consistency.

Leaving the grunt work to obedient villagers is clearly far easier than scheming against your self-important peers. Now you can devote more of your energy to the research that matters.
mystery_dynamics.research.alchemy_worksh:
Alchemy is a lucrative but extremely dangerous craft. One wrong step and you and your crucible will be flying into the sky together.

But faced with huge profits and a shortage of materials, risk has never been a reason to stop production. You consolidated the safety procedures and decided to license part of the work to the big-noses; strict liability waivers and accident compensation contracts are, of course, essential.

As a safety measure, you gave them a lightweight crucible that is just enough for the job, protective gear, and foolproof, simplified recipes.

In exchange, the villagers supply you with materials at close to cost.
mystery_dynamics.research.cooperative_wo:
Compared with the obscure formulas and material ratios of thaumaturgy, plain mechanical engineering has a far lower barrier to entry.

The big-noses don't need to understand load analysis or airtight seals; they just copy the blueprints and quickly get the hang of assembly. Even a complete novice can handle these tedious tasks.

One of your partners was very interested when he heard about this and wants to try hiring villagers in his own workshop to boost output. To keep a crowd of beginners from turning his equipment into scrap, he ordered a set of durable workstations from you and paid with some technical documents.

In return you agreed to charge a friendly processing fee and use your well-established production line to build the workstations in bulk for him.

Pictured: first on the right, the partner leading the villagers towards a bright future.
tc.research_text.MECHANIST_WORKSTATION: There must be a reason mechanists love green robes
mystery_dynamics.research.mechanist_work:
There's no great mystery to building a workstation: make a table out of sturdy materials, fit a few durable machining tools on top, and a complete workstation is done.

But while talking with the villagers you noticed something curious: these mechanists, who spend all day with gears, have an almost obsessive passion for green robes.

You have no idea what this strange trade custom is based on, but it doesn't affect the delivery of equipment or products. As long as the goods arrive on time, who cares what colour the tinkerers wear?
